subject: Region-aware retention toggle and fallback: API + admin contract
messages:
From: Jessica Cole <compliance@pharmaco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@pharmaco-legal.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency + retention: high-level needs and questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking a call last week. To summarize our security and compliance team’s asks for Redwood:

- We need per-tenant configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days + custom) with admin toggles.
- Stored data must be pinned to a regional zone (US-only) unless a customer opts into cross-region replication.
- When a region is temporarily unavailable, we require an explicit fallback policy (either queue + retry, or fail open to secondary US zone) and an auditable decision record.

Attached is a short requirements PDF. Can you confirm whether these are supported today, and if not, what the roadmap and timelines look like? Also: what admin-level APIs would we call to set policy and how are legal holds honored?

Appreciate a quick note back — our board expects a recommended path by the end of next week.

Best,
Jessica Cole
Head of Compliance
Pharmaco Therapeutics
(attachment: pharmaco-retention-requirements.pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Cole <compliance@pharmaco.com>
Cc: legal@pharmaco-legal.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + retention: high-level needs and questions

Jessica — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Short answer: we don’t have tenant-level admin toggles for retention and region-pinning in GA today, but we have a design proposal that maps closely to what you describe.

I attached a one-page API sketch (proposed-api-contract-v1.md) and a short internal timeline. Key notes up front:
- Admin API: PUT /tenants/{id}/retention-policy to set retention_policy_id (predefined policies) or a custom TTL in days.
- Storage zone: POST /tenants/{id}/storage-zone to pin tenant to a region.
- Fallback behavior: configurable policy enum {queue, fail_to_secondary, fail_request} with an audit log event recording the decision and reasoning.
- Legal hold: legal holds should suspend TTL enforcement and be queryable via GET /tenants/{id}/legal-holds.

I’ll loop in product and infra to scope feasibility and estimate. Can we schedule a 30-minute internal sync tomorrow to decide trade-offs (consistent reads vs strict residency during failover)?

— Hannah
Director, Product Mgmt — Redwood Inference
(attachment: proposed-api-contract-v1.md)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Pharmaco ask — scope for configurable retention + region pinning (please advise)

Team — forwarding Pharmaco's requirements and our high-level API sketch. We need to decide scope and minimal acceptance criteria for an initial alpha we can offer to security-sensitive customers.

Objective: provide per-tenant retention toggles + region pinning with documented fallback behavior and auditability. Must-haves for alpha:
- Admin API surface for setting policy (as in attached sketch).
- Enforcement path in serving runtime so TTL purge jobs respect legal holds and policy overrides.
- Admin UI: basic toggle + policy dropdown for workspace owners.
- Audit events for any fallback that routes data or requests outside a tenant's pinned region (timestamp, reason, operator).

Questions for engineering:
1) Can we implement a storage-zone tag at tenant-level that reliably pins writes to US-only allocation? What about KV-cache collisions when we have multi-zone replicas?
2) For failover, do we implement (A) queue writes and retry until region healthy, (B) fail to a designated secondary US zone, or (C) allow cross-region routing with an explicit temporary consent flag? Trade-offs documented below.
3) Estimated effort and earliest canary date (alpha) if we scope to: API + single-region enforcement + audit events (no admin UI).

Trade-offs (brief):
- Queue + retry: strongest residency guarantee but increases tail latency and potential loss if queue grows. Requires durable queueing component.
- Fail to secondary: lower latency but technically moves data to another zone — requires explicit contract with customer (consent).
- Temporary consent flag: flexible but risky for compliance-conscious customers.

Please reply with clarifying questions and rough estimates. I’ll consolidate and propose a roadmap.

Thanks — Hannah

(Quoted: external Pharmaco email above)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Pharmaco ask — scope for configurable retention + region pinning (please advise)

Hannah — good framing. High level answers and notes: 

1) Tenant-level storage-zone tag: feasible. Implementation plan: use metadata on tenant record, propagate tag to allocation scheduler and storage-provisioner. For serving runtime, attach zone on write-time metadata so purge jobs and backups use the tag. Main blocker: cross-tenant GPUs serving multiple tenants will need careful KV cache scoping (we can keep KV cache resident on the same zone by sharding caches by tenant zone id).

2) Failover options: I recommend shipping with option (A) queue + retry for alpha with a configurable max queue TTL. Reasons: preserves residency guarantee, easier to explain to compliance. Operational complexity: we need a light-weight durable queue (SQS/Rabbit) with backpressure policy and alerting. Option (B) (fail to secondary) should be an explicit opt-in per tenant and requires a contract update.

3) Effort estimate for alpha (API + enforcement + audit events, no admin UI): ~6 engineer-weeks (2 infra, 2 runtime, 2 platform) to deliver a canary for a single region (US) + basic e2e test harness. If we add admin UI and multi-zone canary, add 3 more weeks.

Open implementation details:
- API contract field names: retention_policy_id, custom_ttl_days, storage_zone_id, fallback_policy (enum: QUEUE, FAIL_TO_SECONDARY, CROSS_REGION_CONSENT), legal_hold_id.
- Audit log design: append-only events with event_type {FALLBACK_INVOCATION, POLICY_CHANGE, LEGAL_HOLD_APPLIED} and link to operator id + correlation_id. Store events in write-once long-retention store (28+ days).

Risks:
- Backpressure/queue growth during region outage; need throttling and operator playbook.
- Legal hold semantics across purge jobs must be globally visible to all purge workers. We'll add a central legal-hold index service.

If y'all agree, I’ll start a ticket and we can prioritize hiring a short-term infra contractor to accelerate the queue component.

— Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

(On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 09:08 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:)

Subject: Re: Internal: Pharmaco ask — scope for configurable retention + region pinning (please advise)

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clear recommendations. Decision summary and next steps for roadmap: 

Decision: Ship an alpha that supports per-tenant retention toggles + tenant storage-zone pinning for US region with QUEUE fallback by default. Provide an explicit opt-in path for FAIL_TO_SECONDARY (legal/CS signoff required).

Scope for alpha (MVP):
- API: retention + storage-zone endpoints (contract fields Karthik listed).
- Runtime: enforce TTL/purge, honor legal holds, durable queue for write buffering during regional outage.
- Observability: audit events for policy changes and fallback invocations; basic dashboard in Console (no fancy UX).
- Docs: short playbook for customers + operator runbook for outage handling.

Owners & ETA:
- Karthik: technical lead for runtime changes (canary in 6 weeks).
- Aditya: infra lead for durable queue + allocation changes (supporting infra in 6 weeks).
- Hannah: product lead for contract, docs, customer communications (coordinate pilot with Pharmaco).

Action items:
- Karthik: open ticket INF-2314 with subtasks and initial design by EOD Friday.
- Aditya: evaluate queue tech choices (SQS vs internal durable queue) and cost implications.
- Hannah: prepare customer pilot proposal and legal opt-in language for fail-to-secondary.

Lauren
Group PM — Platform
